statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-114158 (GHSA-r8h3-p8p6-ggp7) is a .NET remote code execution issue: a Portable PDB EmbeddedSource record with parent RID 0 can trigger an out-of-bounds write in Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native, the native Windows PDB reader bundled with .NET on Windows. Microsoft lists only Windows (x86, x64 and Arm64) as affected: .NET installed on Windows and the Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.win-* runtime packs, fixed in .NET 10.0.15 (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-r8h3-p8p6-ggp7, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/520). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.24 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries; 10.0.15-r0 is built from the dotnet/dotnet v10.0.115 source tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v10.0.115). Scanned all 154 packages of the seven published builds (10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.12-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside their nupkg and tar.gz archives: none of them contains a Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native file, none contains a native Windows PE file or a Mach-O file, and every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly with a CLR header. They do carry Microsoft.DiaSymReader.dll, a managed .NET assembly, in the dotnet-format and dotnet-watch tools of the bootstrap SDK and as a NuGet package in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts; the advisory does not list that package.
